Context/Background:
Prostate cancer (PCa) is the second leading cause of male cancer-related deaths. To date, the strategy to develop therapies for PCa mainly focuses on blocking either the activity or the transcriptional targets of known oncogenes. While the PCa transcriptome has been studied for decades, we have little knowledge of the translatome. The importance of this post-transcriptional regulation is underscored by the realization that RNA transcript levels are a poor proxy for protein abundance.

Translation initiation is a tightly regulated step critical to maintain the accurate protein dosage of growth and survival factors in cells.Importantly, emerging studies show that translation factors act in a rapid, selective, and robust manner to control the production of specific proteins. One of the most important of those factors is the RNA-binding protein and translation factor eukaryotic initiation factor 4A (eIF4A), which helps to unwind structured 5′ UTRs to increase translation initiation of select mRNAs in cancer.

Pharmacologic inhibition of eIF4A with zotatifin, a clinical compound, suppressed tumor growth in vivo, reducing both primary tumor growth and metastasis.

To understand how the inhibitor works mechanistically, we investigated the effect of zotatifin on the PCa translatome and proteome after a short treatment, as translation is one of the most rapid steps of gene expression. We performed ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) and MS after 6 h of zotatifin treatment in 22Rv1 cell xenografts in vivo. While MS analysis assesses the effect of zotatifin on the global protein landscape in tumors, Ribo-seq can capture translation efficiency genome-wide at single-nucleotide resolution. Ribo-seq analysis revealed 554 downregulated transcripts at the translational level (false discovery rate [FDR] < 0.01 and log2FC ≤ −0.3). On the other hand, MS analysis showed that 339 proteins were downregulated upon zotatifin treatment (p value < 0.05 and log2FC ≤ −0.2). Next, we analyzed genes that are downregulated at the translational level as well as at the protein level by cross-referencing the two datasets using less stringent cutoffs (Ribo-seq FDR < 0.05 and log2FC < 0 and MS p value < 0.05 and log2(FC) < 0).
Prompt: From the genes that are downregulated at both translational level and protein level, prioritize a few targets that are particularly relevant to prostate cancer.
output_text:
Introduction/Context Zotatifin, a selective eIF4A inhibitor, was administered for 6 h to 22Rv1 prostate cancer xenografts. Translation (Ribo-seq) and protein (MS) profiling revealed 554 translationally downregulated transcripts (FDR < 0.01, log₂FC ≤ –0.3) and 339 proteins downregulated (p < 0.05, log₂FC ≤ –0.2). Cross-referencing with less stringent cutoffs (Ribo-seq FDR < 0.05 & log₂FC < 0; MS p < 0.05 & log₂FC < 0) yielded 108 genes down at both layers. Key details not specified in the source: exact replicate number, full clinical metadata. Keywords • eIF4A / translation initiation • Prostate cancer (PCa) • Translatome / proteome integration • Hypoxia signaling Candidate Genes AR, HIF1A, PDCD4, CDK6, PEG10, MCM8 Prioritized Targets Based on dual downregulation, known PCa relevance, and mechanistic tractability: | Gene | Direction | Role / Function | Pathway(s) | |---------|----------------|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------| | PDCD4 | ↓ translatome
↓ proteome | Tumor suppressor that binds eIF4A, inhibits cap-dependent initiation; down in aggressive PCa | Translation regulation | | HIF1A | ↓ translatome
↓ proteome | Master hypoxia response TF; drives angiogenesis, metabolic reprogramming in PCa | Hypoxia signaling | | AR | ↓ translatome
↓ proteome | Androgen receptor; central driver of PCa growth; ETS-fusion target | Androgen response | | CDK6 | ↓ proteome
mild ↑ translatome | G₁–S cyclin-dependent kinase; implicated in castration-resistance | Cell cycle, G₁/S checkpoint | | PEG10 | ↓ translatome
↓ proteome | Imprinted oncofetal protein; promotes proliferation and resistance in PCa | Cell proliferation | | MCM8 | ↓ translatome
↓ proteome | DNA replication licensing factor; links to genomic instability in PCa | DNA replication | Implications & Analysis 1. eIF4A blockade preferentially suppresses translation of structured 5′UTR-rich mRNAs, including PDCD4—a homeostatic eIF4A inhibitor—creating a feed-forward reduction in cap-dependent initiation. 2. Concomitant downregulation of HIF1A suggests impaired hypoxia adaptation, which may sensitize tumors to microenvironmental stress. 3. AR and CDK6 reductions indicate that zotatifin impacts both hormone signaling and cell-cycle progression, offering a multi-pronged antitumor mechanism. 4. PEG10 and MCM8 loss point to decreased proliferative and replicative capacity, reinforcing growth arrest. Targeted (Keyword-Guided) Findings – “Hypoxia” pathways (e.g., HIF-1 signaling) were enriched among downregulated proteins. – “Translation” regulators (PDCD4) surfaced as both a direct and indirect target of eIF4A inhibition. Next Steps & Clarification 1. Validate direct eIF4A-dependent translation of PDCD4 and AR via 5′UTR reporter assays. 2. Test whether rescuing PDCD4 expression modulates sensitivity to zotatifin in vitro. 3. Assess combination of zotatifin with AR-axis inhibitors in castration-resistant PCa models. 4. Clarify whether hypoxia-induced HIF1A downregulation correlates with reduced angiogenesis in vivo.
